name: BMW M3 (E30)
torque: 170 lb-ft @ 4,750 rpm (US catalyzed; Euro non-cat cars made ~200 hp)
transmission: 5-speed manual (Getrag 265, dogleg) — no automatic was ever offered
reliability: 8/10 — the S14 is a race-bred, over-built four (its head is essentially half of the M88/S38 straight-six) and will run for decades if maintained, but this is a hand-built homologation special from the late '80s, so 'maintained' means real work. It wants periodic valve-lash shim adjustments, fresh timing-chain guides, and a specialist who knows the S14's throttle bodies and idle control. The bigger risk on any E30 is rust. A sorted, rust-free car is a blue-chip collectible now, and that changes the ownership math entirely — you preserve it, you don't thrash it.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (appreciating classic — agreed-value collector policy recommended) · Maintenance ~$1,500/yr and specialist-dependent; S14-specific parts are scarce and pricey · A genuine appreciating asset where originality and documented history drive value
popular_mods: A meticulous suspension refresh with period-correct or quality dampers and fresh bushings
A proper rust repair and respray — the single most value-adding 'mod' on any E30 M3
A rebuilt or correctly-tuned throttle body / idle-control setup for crisp S14 response
Subtle wheel/tire freshening in the correct offsets; resist over-modifying a collectible
Honest take: a numbers-matching, unmolested E30 M3 is worth far more than any modified one — preserve, don't personalize
oil_type: 20W-50 (period spec); many owners now run a quality 10W-60 or 20W-50 synthetic

generations.E30 M3 (1986–1991): The original — a boxy-fendered Group A touring-car homologation special with the high-strung S14 four spinning near a 7,000 rpm redline. Light, analog, quick-steering, and the car that founded the entire M3 legend. US cars arrived with catalytic converters and slightly less power than Europe's.
generations.Evolution models (Euro-only): Europe received progressively hotter Evo II and Sport Evolution (2.5L, ~238 hp) homologation runs never sold in the US — the most collectible E30 M3s of all.

common_issues: Timing-chain guide and tensioner wear if service is deferred — a known S14 item
Requires periodic valve-lash (shim) adjustment to run right and protect the valvetrain
Valve-stem seals weep with age, causing blue smoke on cold startup
S14-specific parts scarcity and finicky idle-control/throttle-body behavior
Classic E30 rust — strut towers, rockers, rear arches, and trunk floor
maintenance_tips: Use a specialist who knows the S14 — it is not a generic BMW four
Keep valve clearances and timing-chain guides on schedule; both are cheaper than the failures they prevent
Inspect thoroughly for rust before buying, and address any early corrosion aggressively
Warm the engine before revving it hard, and use a suitable high-ZDDP or 10W-60/20W-50 oil
Preserve originality and paperwork — with the market where it is, correctness is the value

engine.detail: 2.3L S14B23 DOHC 16v inline-four - essentially half of the M88/S38 six - ~192 hp US (Euro non-cat ~200) spinning to a ~7,000 rpm redline.
engine.watch: Timing-chain guide/tensioner rails wear by ~80-100k, it needs periodic valve-lash shim checks, and valve-stem seals weep (blue smoke on cold start).

drivetrain.detail: RWD through a dogleg Getrag 265 five-speed manual - an automatic was never offered.
drivetrain.watch: The dogleg gate and worn shifter bushings feel notchy with age; the clutch and diff are stout, so mostly just check for driveline slack.

suspension.detail: MacPherson-strut front, semi-trailing-arm rear and a quick-ratio steering rack - the light, analog homologation chassis that started the M3 name.
suspension.watch: On 30-plus-year-old cars the dampers, bushings and subframe mounts are usually tired; a full refresh with quality parts transforms it.

brakes.detail: Four-wheel discs, vented up front, sized for a sub-2,900 lb car - modest by modern standards but plenty for the weight.
brakes.watch: Nothing chronic; on cars that sit, watch for seized calipers and perished flex lines, and refresh any old brake fluid.

body.detail: The boxy, flared-fender Group A homologation shell unique to the E30 M3 - steel with bespoke wide-body panels.
body.watch: Rust is the E30 killer: check strut towers, rockers, rear arches and trunk floor - a rust-free shell is where the value lives.
